business_model.claim: The company runs two lines of business, social casino games and real-money online casino services (iGaming), and reports them as two operating segments.
quotes: We operate two lines of businesses: (i) social casino games; and (ii) online casino services which offer games typically available in land-based casinos such as blackjack, roulette, and slot machines (“iGaming”).
We have two operating segments, (i) social casino games; and (ii) iGaming.

business_model.claim: Social casino games are free to play. Nearly all social casino revenue comes from players buying extra virtual chips, which cannot be redeemed for money.
quotes: We generate substantially all of our social casino revenue from the sale of additional virtual chips, which players can choose to purchase at any time to enhance their playing experience.
Our virtual chips cannot be withdrawn from the game, transferred from one game to another or from one player to another, or be redeemed for monetary value.

business_model.claim: iGaming revenue comes from customers' real-money play. It is recognized on amounts wagered net of expected winnings and bonuses, not on deposits.
quotes: At that point, revenue is recognized based on the amount wagered, which is defined as the total amount staked by customers, net of expected winnings, and any promotional bonuses.

business_model.claim: iGaming segment revenue grew to 60,980 in 2025 from 33,051 in 2024, while social casino revenue fell to $298,958 from $308,279. The segment table prints no scale.

quotes: SuprNation contributed a total revenue of $61 millions for the year ended December 31, 2025, representing approximately 17% of our total revenue for 2025.

business_model.claim: Revenue depends on a small share of players who pay. The social casino payer conversion rate rose from 6.7% in 2024 to 8.2% in 2025.
quotes: We rely on a small percentage of our players for all of our revenue.

business_model.claim: Revenue is concentrated in the DoubleDown Casino title, though the share fell to 76.1% in 2025 from 88.6% in 2024.
quotes: Historically, DoubleDown Casino has accounted for a significant majority of our revenue (2025: 76.1%; 2024: 88.6%), and we expect that this dependency will continue for the foreseeable future while we endeavor to further diversify our portfolio through the addition of new games.

business_model.claim: Social casino games are sold mainly through third-party platforms such as Apple, Facebook, Google and Amazon. These platforms take a fixed percentage fee and pay the company net.
quotes: These platforms typically charge us a fixed percentage fee for their payment processing and other services, and remit payments to us net of their fees.

business_model.claim: The share of revenue from players on third-party platforms fell to 79.8% in 2025 from 90.0% in 2024 as company-owned channels grew.
quotes: Historically, a significant majority of our revenue was generated by players using those platforms (2025: 79.8%; 2024: 90.0%), although revenue from purchases made through company-owned channels, including web storefront transactions and other direct payment flows, continued to increase over the recent years.

business_model.claim: Direct-to-Consumer revenue rose to $121.4 from $63.7, and third-party platform revenue fell to $238.5 from $277.6 (table in millions). DTC was 33.7% of revenue in 2025 against 18.7% in 2024.
quotes: Approximately 33.7% of our revenue was attributable to our DTC channels in 2025, which increased significantly as compared to 18.7% in 2024.

business_model.claim: The DTC shift continued in Q3 2026. DTC revenue reached $44.6 million, or 58.0% of social casino revenue, against $16.6 million and 20.9% in Q3 2025.
quotes: DTC revenue as a percentage of total social casino revenue increased to 58.0% in the third quarter of 2026 from 20.9% in the third quarter of 2025 and 52.4% in the second quarter of 2026.

business_model.claim: Cost of revenue consists of payment processing fees, royalties, customer service and hosting. Platform fees are the largest part: $80.7 in 2025 against $89.0 in 2024 (table in millions).
quotes: Cost of revenue includes payment processing fees, royalties, customer service, and hosting fees.

business_model.claim: Growth in DTC revenue reduced platform fees and lowered cost of revenue.
quotes: Cost of revenue decreased by 1.9% from $103.5 million in 2024 to $101.5 million in 2025, primarily as a result of a decrease in platform fees as our DTC revenue continued to grow.

growth_thesis.claim: Driver: social casino revenue is shifting to company-owned direct-to-consumer (DTC) channels. DTC was approximately 33.7% of annual revenue versus 18.7% a year earlier.
quotes: Approximately 33.7% of our revenue was attributable to our DTC channels in 2025, which increased significantly as compared to 18.7% in 2024.

growth_thesis.claim: The DTC shift accelerated in the latest quarter. DTC reached 58.0% of social casino revenue, up from 20.9% a year earlier and 52.4% in the prior quarter.
quotes: DTC revenue as a percentage of total social casino revenue increased to 58.0% in the third quarter of 2026 from 20.9% in the third quarter of 2025 and 52.4% in the second quarter of 2026.

growth_thesis.claim: The DTC mix lowers cost of revenue and lifts operating profit. Cost of revenue fell from 30.3% to 28.2% of annual revenue, and quarterly operating profit rose to $37.5 million from $35.0 million.
quotes: Cost of revenue as a percentage of revenue decreased by 2.1 percentage points from 30.3% in 2024 to 28.2% in 2025, due to increased utilization of our DTC channels.

These factors were partially offset by higher operating profit, which increased to $37.5 million from $35.0 million, driven by lower cost of revenue attributable to a higher proportion of DTC revenue.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated as a risk factor in the cited item; its link to the DTC driver is inferred.

Revenue from SuprNation, the Company’s iGaming subsidiary, increased 7.4% year-over-year to $17.4 million, primarily as a result of the continued success of the Company’s newest brand, Los Vegas.
